svg.text: Five ways to make the search index smaller, priced — and the one sentence that refuses all five
Each applied to the real words of all thirty-five pages and priced off the live index. Room is for a page in The runtime, 11 November 2026.
words of room it would leave the next page — the site has 373 today
WHAT EACH SAVING BUYS, AND WHAT IT SPENDS IT OUT OF
a repeated body stored once
no two bodies on this site are identical
373 words
bill 79,339 gzipped · costs the reader: nothing — and it buys nothing
a repeated sentence stored once
a fifteenth of the stored text, 16,598 bytes
483 words
bill 79,146 gzipped · costs the reader: the row: eighteen doors stop answering
lower-casing the stored words
the Gate → the gate
1,208 words
bill 77,863 gzipped · costs the reader: the excerpt's capitals
dropping the punctuation
a shop. “Change… → a shop Change…
2,674 words
bill 75,273 gzipped · costs the reader: the excerpt's punctuation
dropping the commonest function words
a quarter of every stored sentence
11,114 words
bill 60,352 gzipped · costs the reader: the excerpt, as a sentence at all
WHAT THE LARGEST ONE WOULD SHOW A READER WHO TYPED “no second way in”
today
A confirmation is not a way past the Gate. When a person says yes, the change is judged again —…
instead
confirmation way past Gate. When person says yes, change judged again — policy resolved again…
A body is not only matched. It is shown — so every saving over the stored words buys its bytes out of the row a reader reads.
Which leaves the four candidates in 0353: they change which bodies travel, not how they are written. Priced in _lib/search/savings.ts.
